entries.title: Root shell with listener/reverse-shell heuristics (PID {pid})
entries.description: A process running as root has command-line indicators of a listening or reverse shell.
entries.impact: If this is unauthorised it is a likely backdoor providing persistent root access; if authorised it is a maintenance task and can be marked false-positive after verification.
entries.remediation_brief: Verify the process; if unauthorised, kill it (kill -9 <pid>) and investigate parent process tree for persistence.

entries.title: High-risk service listening as root on port {port}
entries.description: A historically-exploitable service is listening as root.
entries.impact: Compromise of the service results in root execution. Specifically risky for FTP/Telnet (cleartext), NFS, RDBMS, Redis/MongoDB/Memcached (frequently misconfigured), and Elasticsearch (historical default no-auth).
entries.remediation_brief: Run the service as a non-root user; bind to loopback only when not externally needed; confirm authentication and firewall rules.

entries.title: Setuid binary not owned by root: {path}
entries.description: A setuid binary is owned by a non-root user.
entries.impact: Compromising the file owner allows arbitrary modification of the binary, which then executes with the owner's UID (and any setuid escalation it performs) on the next invocation. Classic local-privesc pattern.
entries.remediation_brief: chown root:root <path> + audit why the binary is setuid; remove suid bit if not strictly required (chmod u-s).
